title: Finite type points of spaces have locally finite type field representatives
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $x\in|X|$, where points are field-valued maps modulo equality after common field extension [def-weil-field]. The following are equivalent: (i) there are a scheme $W$, a closed point $w\in W$, and a representable etale map $e:W\to X$ with $e(w)=x$; (ii) there are a field $K$ and a locally finite type map $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ representing $x$. Here etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism], affine spectra are [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and locally of finite type for a space map is tested on compatible etale scheme charts with [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No Noetherian, Jacobson, quasi-compactness or separatedness assumption is imposed on $S$ or $X$.

source.place: Tag 06EF (lemma-point-finite-type), conditions (1) and (2); Tag 06EH (lemma-identify-finite-type-points) restates the chart characterization.

proof.text: Assume (i). Put $k=\kappa(w)$ and let $c:\operatorname{Spec}k\to W$ be the canonical map. Choose an affine open neighbourhood of $w$ in $W$. Since $w$ is closed in $W$, it is closed in that affine open, and the residue extension for $c$ is $k/k$, of degree one. The scheme field-point criterion therefore makes $c$ locally of finite type. The chartwise calculus, applied to algebraic spaces viewed as discrete algebraic stacks, makes $e$ locally of finite type (etale implies smooth, then locally of finite presentation, then locally of finite type) and makes $e c$ locally of finite type by composition. Its field-valued point class is $e(w)=x$, so $K=k$ and $a=e c$ give (ii).

Assume (ii), and choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $e:U\to X$, which exists by the definition of an algebraic space. Form $V=U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K$, with projections $p:V\to U$ and $q:V\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. The fibre-product and covering theorem gives a scheme $V$ and makes $q$ surjective and etale. In particular $V$ is nonempty, since $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has a point. The map $p$ is the base change of the locally finite type map $a$, so the chartwise calculus makes $p$ locally of finite type as an algebraic-space map. The chart-test theorem identifies this with local finite type for the scheme morphism $p$. We have the equality $e p=a q$.

Choose a nonempty affine open $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq V$. Its coordinate ring is nonzero: a prime ideal corresponding to any point of $V_0$ is proper. The maximal-ideal existence theorem supplies a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$. The associated point $v$ is closed in $V_0$, because its singleton is the closed set $V(\mathfrak m)$: a prime containing a maximal ideal equals that ideal. Put $L=\kappa(v)$. For the canonical map $r:\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$, condition (iii) of the scheme field-point criterion holds on $V_0$, with identity residue extension $L/L$. Thus $r$ is locally of finite type. This explicitly supplies the finite type point of $V$ selected in the source proof; $v$ need not be closed in all of $V$.

The composite $p r:\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$ is locally of finite type by the chartwise composition theorem (which includes scheme morphisms). The scheme field-point criterion gives an affine open $U_0\subseteq U$ containing its image $u$, such that $u$ is closed in $U_0$ (and $L/\kappa(u)$ is finite, though this extra conclusion is not needed). The open inclusion $j:U_0\hookrightarrow U$ is etale by the open-immersion theorem; the chartwise composition theorem makes $e j:U_0\to X$ etale. It is representable: for a scheme $T$ and $T\to X$, the sheaf $T\times_XU_0=(T\times_XU)\times_UU_0$ is the open subscheme of the scheme $T\times_XU$ (representability of $e$) lying over $U_0$. Finally $e p r=a q r$. The map $q r$ is a map of field spectra and hence comes from a field embedding $K\hookrightarrow L$, so $a q r$ is the extension of $a$ to $L$ and represents $x$. On the other hand, by the field-point description of scheme morphisms, $p r=j_u\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ for the canonical $j_u:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ and a field map $\varphi:\kappa(u)\to L$; $j_u$ factors through $U_0$, so $e p r$ is the extension to $L$ of $(e j)\circ j_u$, which represents $(e j)(u)$. Thus $(e j)(u)=x$. Taking $W=U_0$ and $w=u$ proves (i).

First, 'representable by convention' was a bare assertion; I wrote the argument: T×_X U_0 is an open subscheme of T×_X U. Second, the step concluded (ej)(u)=x without relating Spec L→X to the point represented by Spec κ(u)→U_0→X. I added the factorization p r=j_u∘Spec(φ) from the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field (Stacks 01J5) to the step's uses and to proof_deps. Edge cases checked: empty X, Spec k, and the generic point of a DVR, which is closed in its chart but not in X.
